questions.title: Who will be the first major Ukrainian political figure to publicly call for wartime elections following Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion?
questions.background: Ukrainian law bars elections during wartime. The presidential election has been postponed under continuing martial law, although Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s presidential term ended in May 2024.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements corroborated by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Qualifying Event : Identify the person credited in reliable reporting with the first public call by a major Ukrainian political figure since Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion to resume national elections while the war continues. A call solely for elections after the war ends does not qualify. Resolution Timing : Resolve when the qualifying statement becomes public, provided this occurs by August 31, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The politician’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: As of June 2026, Ukrainian martial law bars wartime elections and major opposition leaders (Poroshenko, Tymoshenko, Klitschko) publicly opposed voting during active fighting through early 2026, while Zelenskyy tied elections to a ceasefire and security guarantees (Dec 2025–Feb 2026). If a major political figure breaks this consensus by August 31 amid U.S. pressure and domestic political friction, former president Petro Poroshenko (who already floated voting during a temporary ceasefire) and Yulia Tymoshenko (who held back-channel talks with Trump allies in 2025) are the most likely challengers, followed closely by vocal Zelenskyy critic Vitali Klitschko, Zelenskyy himself if he pivots to preempt rivals under U.S. pressure, and top polling rival Valerii Zaluzhnyi.

local_articles.title: Supreme Court orders Samsung Securities to pay damages to NPS over 2018 dividend error
local_articles.snippet: The Supreme Court on Wednesday ordered Samsung Securities Co. to pay the National Pension Service (NPS) 1.86 billion won ($1.3 million) in damages over a 2018 dividend error by an accidental stock issuance. The top court ruled in favor of the NPS in the damages suit filed against the brokerage firm stemming from a "fat-finger" error committed by an employee at the firm on April 6, 2018. The stock blunder took place when the Samsung Securities official typed in 1,000 shares instead of 1,000 won per share in dividends that were to be paid to employees under a compensation plan. As a result, the company issued 2.8 billion shares worth about 112 trillion won that only existed on paper, and some employees who received the stocks quickly sold them in the market.
